decision_clause: Ruled out: "pin every prose field by literal digest" — freezing the full text duplicates the contract into the validator and makes any editorial fix a false failure; only fields the contract derives or fixes numerically are pinned.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so the implementation introduces no new pinning of any kind. In the tree as it stands, the registry validator compares a metric entry's fields only against values the contract derives or fixes numerically — factor from the M-index band, treatment from the metric id, aggregation and minimum_opportunities from the treatment class, cap === 1, floor === 0, version === the contract-version constant, the numeric confidence table, the ordered evidence-precedence enum, consumer_routes computed from factor/treatment, and per_opportunity_formula reconstructed from the entry's own numerator and denominator strings. Free prose fields (label, question, partial_credit_rule, gaming_guard, not_observed_rule, invalid_rule, normalization, numerator/denominator text) are only checked for presence via the REQUIRED_FIELDS key list and are never compared to a stored literal or hashed. The only sha256 use in scope is scripts/validate-planning.mjs:780 and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:272, which digest whole accepted-gate ticket artifacts for staleness detection — pre-existing file-level gate bookkeeping, not per-field pinning of registry prose.
rationale: The decision forbids one specific validator shape: hard-freezing the literal text of prose fields (by stored string or digest) inside the metric-registry validator, so that an editorial wording fix would fail the check. Nothing in the finished tree does that. The empty diff already settles it — the implementation changed nothing, so it cannot have added the ruled-out mechanism — and reading the tree directly confirms the validator's pins are exactly the class the decision permits: derived (formula from numerator/denominator, routes from factor/treatment) or numerically/enumeratively fixed (cap, floor, confidence table, precedence order, aggregation, minimum_opportunities). Prose fields appear only as membership in a required-key list, which is a completeness check, not a text freeze. The task itself (adding observation_key as a required typed field on the exported MetricDefinition plus a compile-checked consumer) was not carried out — the interface at packages/schema/src/metric-registry.ts:26-51 still omits observation_key even though REQUIRED_FIELDS at line 66 lists it and validateVectors reads metric.observation_key, and no new consumer file exists. That is a failure to deliver the task, not a decision violation; the question asked is only whether the tree implements the ruled-out approach, and it plainly does not. Approving this tree would require no re-explanation of the recorded decision.
